title: How does "7% of the plan" become a budget the hub can stop on?
lead: Should the hub turn the budget percentage into dollars using one figure, dollars per 1% of your week, which it estimates from the logs and you confirm once? I recommend it, with the plan-meter guard beside it: you keep thinking in percent, and the launch screen shows the dollar figure before you launch.
for_you: The launch screen shows the budget as a percentage with its dollar figure beside it; the run stops at whichever trips first: that dollar figure, or your week's meter rising by that many points

Rough figures from Crux's own log: about $9 per point, so 7% is about $63; a full 6-hour run is estimated at $45 to $130 (judgement, not measured), so 7% may stop some runs early. Per-role costs get measured on the first small test run
Spend counts while turns are still running, and stopped agents' last turns are counted, so the stop isn't late

for_you.text: Once: keep or change the hub's estimate of dollars per 1% (one number in hub.json)

for_you: With an API key the meters hide, so the screen shows dollars only
context: Spec section 12, question 1 (memo M044). The hub logs each turn's estimated list-price cost; the plan meter is polled every 5 minutes in tenths of a point and also moves with other work. Crux's own log gives a rough figure (first pass about $2.7 per point, second pass about $9, swinging widely per stretch); other projects' logs are not read. The advisor checkpoint (2026-11-16) found that spend shows only at turn end and that stopped turns are never logged; the build fixes both (spend counted during the turn; agents interrupted, then retired).

options.name: A dollar figure you set once
options.summary: The envelope is set in dollars, for example $20, not percent.
cons: Not tied to your plan; you think in percent

options.name: The hub calibrates by itself
options.summary: The hub keeps measuring how far the meter moves per dollar and converts the percentage silently.
cons: The log is too noisy for this; a wrong factor over- or under-spends without you seeing it

options.name: One confirmed figure, plus the meter guard
options.summary: The hub suggests dollars per 1% of your week from the logs; you keep or change it once. The cap is enforced in dollars, and the plan-meter guard (up 7 points since launch) runs beside it.
pros: You think in percent and see the dollars; two guards, as the spec wants; nothing hidden
cons: One number to confirm, and it may need adjusting after the first runs

recommendation: C: keeps 'percent' as the thing you set while the stop works on dollars it can actually measure.
change_mind: If the first runs show the meter guard always trips first, the dollar figure can be raised; if the reverse, lowered.

settles.value: enforced in estimated dollars from a human-confirmed dollars-per-plan-percent figure, with a plan-meter guard beside it; spend counted during turns
